per_scenario_events.label: good
per_scenario_events.explanation: For the PATIENTS table specifically: get_single_table_schema returned 11 columns (id, family_name, given_name, gender, birth_date, city, state, postal_code, last_updated, resource, partition). The append_nquads calls define exactly one owl:Class (Patient) with a rich, business-meaningful rdfs:comment, businessPurpose, businessConcepts, referenceTables, commonQueryPatterns, sampleData and notes annotations. All 11 columns are modeled as owl:DatatypeProperty with rdfs:domain, rdfs:range, rdfs:label, and detailed rdfs:comment (e.g., birth_date, gender, city, state, postal_code, resource, partition all have specific, non-generic comments). Coverage is complete (axis 1 = strong) and annotation quality is high (axis 3 = strong). Regarding relationship modeling (axis 2): PATIENTS has no FK-like *_REF columns (it is the root/parent entity referenced by other tables), and the session context explicitly states 'FK RELATIONSHIPS: none identified for this table.' The agent correctly did not invent any FK ObjectProperties for PATIENTS itself — the inbound FKs (patient_ref from CONDITIONS, ENCOUNTERS, MEDICATIONS, OBSERVATIONS) were correctly modeled as ObjectProperties on those other tables with range Patients, which is appropriate since PATIENTS is the target, not the source, of those relationships. This satisfies the axis 2 condition of 'table genuinely has no FKs and none are invented.' All three axes are strong for this table, and the persist_file_to_neptune step confirms 80 triples were successfully written to Neptune with no other tables' data mixed in, matching the reported ObjectProperties added: 0 (correct, since PATIENTS has no outbound FKs).
